ruleset.name: Design Rules
ruleset.description: The Design Ruleset contains a collection of rules that find software design related problems. Rust behavior: docs/design.md.

rule.name: ExitExpression
rule.description: An exit-expression within regular code is untestable and therefore it should be avoided. Consider moving the exit call into `main` or a thin startup wrapper that returns an error code to the calling environment. In Rust this means calls to `std::process::exit` or `std::process::abort` (including shorter paths that end in `exit` / `abort`).

rule.name: GotoStatement
rule.description: IDENTITY / QUIET for Rust: the language has no `goto`. The rule remains loadable for catalog parity and never fabricates findings.
rule.example: // No Rust example — goto does not exist.

rule.name: CountInLoopExpression
rule.description: Using `.len()` or `.capacity()` in loop conditions is considered bad practice and is a potential source of bugs, especially when the loop manipulates a collection, as the count is re-evaluated on each iteration. Prefer binding the length once before the loop.

rule.name: DevelopmentCodeFragment
rule.message: The {0} {1}() calls the typical debug function {2}() which is mostly only used during development.
rule.description: Macros and functions like `println!`, `print!`, `eprintln!`, and `dbg!` are normally only used during development and therefore such calls in production code are a good indicator that they were just forgotten.

property.name: unwanted-functions
property.description: Comma-separated list of additional suspect function or macro names (e.g. tracing_debug,todo).

rule.name: EmptyCatchBlock
rule.message: Avoid using empty catch blocks in {0}.
rule.description: Rust has no try/catch. The analog of a swallowed exception is an empty error-handling block: `if let Err(_) = … {}` or an empty `Err(…)` match arm. Usually empty error handlers are a bad idea because you are silently swallowing a failure and then continuing execution.

rule.name: CouplingBetweenObjects
rule.message: The class {0} has a coupling between objects value of {1}. Consider to reduce the number of dependencies under {2}.
rule.description: A type with too many dependencies has negative impacts on several quality aspects. This includes stability, maintainability and understandability. The coupling is measured by counting distinct non-builtin type names referenced in fields, method parameters, and return types.

rule.name: GlobalVariable
rule.description:
ADAPTED: Flags `static mut` items that are actually mutated somewhere in the file (assigned or compound-assigned). Mutable static state hurts testability and is unsafe under concurrency.
By default only statics that are actually mutated are reported. Set the `report-immutable` property to also flag un-mutated `static mut` items.
Immutable `static` and `const` items are never flagged.

property.name: report-immutable
property.description: Also flag static mut items that are never mutated in the file.

rule.name: LackOfCohesionOfMethods
rule.message: The {0} has a Lack of Cohesion Of Methods (LCOM4) value of {1}. Consider to split this class into {1} smaller classes.
rule.description:
Computes the LCOM4 cohesion metric per type. Methods are linked when they share a field or when one calls another via `self`. The metric is the number of disconnected method groups; a value above `maximum` (default 1) means the type bundles unrelated responsibilities and is a candidate for splitting.
Trivial getters and setters are excluded from the graph; a call to a getter counts as use of its backing field. Stateless methods (no field use, no sibling calls) are ignored so data carriers with accessors are not falsely flagged.

property.name: maximum
property.description: The maximum number of allowed LCOM4 components.
